A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATLAS work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding experiments and examples can be matched despite added material and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original dataset-generation, benchmark, and ablation results. Appendix B reports human evaluation of the validation pipeline.

after.justification: V3 retains the original empirical results and adds fine-tuning comparisons, miniF2F evaluation, and original dataset-quality analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The concept extraction, teacher-student synthesis, compilation/alignment, proof and contraposition augmentation, and iterative training pipeline remain unchanged. Added backbone and fine-tuning configurations are experimental variants; curriculum and dependency-aware generation remain future work.

E1.justification: Table 4 adds miniF2F evaluation while retaining ProofNet, PutnamBench, and MathQual. The training corpora and natural-language-to-Lean statement formalization task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The main comparison and Appendix B retain their baseline sets. However, the stronger-backbone comparison moves from v2 Table 2, with four baselines, to v3 Table 4, which includes only Herald Translator and Kimina-Autoformalizer; DeepSeek-V3 and Llama3.1-Initialization remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: Section 4.2.4 substantially expands experimental controls through LoRA versus full-parameter fine-tuning across Llama, DeepSeek-Prover, and Qwen-Coder backbones. Appendix A adds 100-proposition panel-voting and BLEU-analysis protocols. Existing benchmark metrics and the compilation/back-translation/NLI pipeline are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses of backbone and fine-tuning dependence, the truthfulness of generated propositions, and the relative diversity of proof versus contraposition augmentation. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence beyond the retained component ablations, validation-error study, and case studies.

E5.justification: Five-seed averaging and two-sided t-tests remain unchanged. However, the retained DeepSeek LoRA variant loses its per-score significance annotations when moved from v2 Table 2 to v3 Table 4, where asterisks instead denote full-parameter fine-tuning.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds miniF2F scores and additional tuning variants, including 54.99% ProofNet pass@1 for full-parameter DeepSeek. Appendix A newly reports 60 true versus 40 false sampled propositions and BLEU averages of 0.6709 versus 0.6026. Original benchmark, ablation, human-evaluation, and ATLAS Translator† scores are retained, with the latter renamed ATLAS Translator (D).

T1.justification: Neither version provides formal theoretical results about ATLAS. The contraposition reasoning and mathematical/Lean examples are unchanged; the new audits and future-work proposals introduce no proofs or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution 3 newly emphasize superior performance from full-parameter fine-tuning of a stronger backbone. The central framework, 117k-statement dataset, MathQual, and translator contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Appendix A expands the earlier nonverification caveat into substantive discussion of downstream risks from false propositions, limited diversity from trivial proof tactics, and curriculum/dependency-aware extensions. Section 4.2.4 also adds interpretations of backbone effects and a broad claim of full-parameter tuning superiority.

D1.justification: V2 promises a future release; v3 supplies a repository link and states that datasets, model, and code are available, although checklist item 13 contradictorily says no new assets have been released. Core hyperparameters, hardware information, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a focused comparison with the already-cited MUSTARD, distinguishing concept sourcing and generation efficiency, and discusses complementarity with RAutoformalizer. References to curriculum learning and miniF2F are added; the main related-work taxonomy is retained.

P1.justification: V3 makes local grammatical and terminology edits, updates author/affiliation text, adds Section 4.2.4 and a NeurIPS checklist, and reorganizes Appendix A into motivation, limitations, and future work. Most existing prose and Appendix B-F content remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 4, transfers the existing DeepSeek variant into it, adjusts Table 2's structure and captions, and renumbers subsequent tables. Figures 1-5 and the appendix example displays are retained, with limited placement and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: The added tuning comparisons and dataset-quality audits strengthen the evidence and make previously qualitative limitations concrete. Clearer positioning against MUSTARD also helps. These gains are limited by sparse details for the new fine-tuning configurations and overbroad interpretation: the claim of consistent full-parameter superiority overlooks miniF2F exceptions, including Qwen pass@32 of 96.72% with LoRA versus 92.62% with full tuning.
